claims.claim: A 29-inch LG TV is for sale.
claims.evidence: Witness photos show a dark glossy large kitchen appliance with a curved front edge and a vent/grille side panel—described as a refrigerator or similar large appliance—not a TV.

claims.claim: It’s the transformer that got blown up.
claims.evidence: No TV/transformer evidence is shown in the witness report; the photos do not indicate a TV or any transformer component.

claims.claim: No dead pixel, no line on the screen, remote included.
claims.evidence: The witness report does not show a TV screen or any display/lines/dead pixels, and does not confirm the remote.
No repair history evidence (service marks, opened casing, receipts) is shown in the witness report.

risks.risk: Item identity mismatch: the photos appear to be a refrigerator/large kitchen appliance, not a 29-inch LG TV.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the front of the TV showing the screen and bezel (and/or the LG logo), plus a photo of the back/ports and the model/rating label.
risks.if_unproven: Price as the worst-case for a non-matching item (treat as not the TV described; assume unusable for TV purpose).

risks.risk: If it is a TV, the seller claims a blown transformer, which typically means no power or no proper operation; cooling/working status cannot be inferred from the current photos.
risks.proof: A short video showing power-on attempt (plug in, power button, any standby light), and a screen-on test (even a blank backlight is evidence).
risks.if_unproven: Price as not working / faulty electronics.

risks.risk: Remote and accessories may be missing or not included.
risks.proof: Photo of the remote in hand next to the TV (or in the same frame), and a photo of all accessories/shelves/bins if it’s actually a refrigerator.

risks.risk: Condition issues (dents, scratches, rust, broken seals/missing parts) are not shown.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all sides and corners, plus the rating plate/serial label and any visible damage.
risks.if_unproven: Price as cosmetically used with possible minor damage.

proof_requests: Send clear photos that confirm the item is a TV: front screen (powered off and powered on), and the back panel with ports.
Send the LG rating/model label (serial/model/country) and the exact screen size confirmation.
Send a short power-on video showing whether it turns on (standby light/backlight) and whether there is any display.
Send a photo of the remote included (remote in the same frame as the TV).
If it is actually a refrigerator/large appliance, send photos of the rating plate, interior, and any faults (cooling performance).
response.reason: The witness photos do not match the seller’s claim of a 29-inch LG TV; without proof of the actual item and working/power status, a reliable worst-case price cannot be set.
